To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

combinatorial assembly and rational selection of homologous transcription devices from different species of bacteria can significantly increase the dynamic control space in synthetic mammalian gene expression devices.

the combinatorial assembly and rational choice of regulatory elements from different species, in this case bacterial species, can be used to create a broad range of regulatory genetic circuits that are capable of controlling gene expression in a desired and predefined manner.
the combination of different regulatory elements, originating from different bacterial species, can be used to create novel regulatory systems with predefined properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel and powerful methodology for the combinatorial design of mammalian regulatory devices based on bacterial transcription factors.

the development of a combinatorial assembly strategy for constructing mammalian transcription devices from prokaryotic transcription elements and with the identification and characterization of new mammalian transcription devices.

the development of a novel methodology to construct and optimize mammalian transcriptional regulatory devices, which are composed of prokaryotic regulatory modules and are based on the combinatorial assembly and rational optimization of different regulatory elements from the same or from different species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
combinatorial assembly and optimization of regulatory elements from different species, can significantly expand the design space for the construction of synthetic mammalian transcription devices.
combinatorial assembly and selection of transcriptional devices can increase the dynamic control space in mammalian genetic circuits.
the combination of different bacterial transcription devices, fused to e.g. a mammalian transactivation domain, results in a broad spectrum of dynamic regulatory profiles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have increased the dynamic control space for mammalian transcription devices, by combinatorial design and assembly of homologus regulatory elements from different bacteria, and that this approach is applicable for a wide range of transcriptional regulatory devices.
the combinatorial assembly and optimization of regulatory devices can increase the diversity and the control space of mammalians cells.

combinatorial assembly and rational design of transcriptional devices, composed by homologous promoter/transactivator modules from different bacterial species, is a powerful strategy to increase the diversity and dynamic control space of regulatory genetic circuits in mammalian cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combinatorial assembly approach can increase the dynamic control space for transcriptional devices, which can be utilized in a variety of applications.
the design of regulatory genetic circuits can be improved by combining different regulatory elements from different species.

combinatorial engineering of homologous transcriptional regulatory elements from different prokaryotic species is a powerful approach to create a large variety of mammalian transcriptional devices with diverse regulatory properties.
